response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, stable termination, and derived initial-entry defects. Closed FCSTM shows: root [*] -> HumanDriving (reachable, tr line13), HumanDriving <-> Autonomous reachable pair, AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive reachable, and AutonomousFinal reachable but with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic, verify_facts deadlock check refuted). NL5-TERM-1 requires a genuine terminal transition to a Final state on power-off; the closed model does route HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal on Power_Off and AutonomousFinal has no outgoing edge, so the reachable leaf is a true dead end with no re-entry or cycling -- this satisfies the termination obligation rather than violating it (no re-entry, no exit to another operating scope). All six declared events have a reachable consumer transition per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, so no NL contract here needs an event-consumer-coverage candidate. The composite Autonomous is flat in FCSTM (no owned entry semantics beyond a single transition to AutonomousIdle-like state named Autonomous itself, which is a leaf state, not a submachine with children in the closed model) -- so the NL2-DERIVED-97da8afc74902d28e3c0 owner-local initial-entry obligation cannot be satisfied because the closed model collapses AutonomousMode/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/auto-final into sibling leaf states with no owning composite state and no owner-local initial pseudostate edge for an 'Autonomous' composite. This is the key behavioral defect: AutonomousMode is required as a composite owning substates (NL2-DECL-1, already handled by contract_structure_contrast lens) and required to have an owner-local default entry (derived contract), but the closed FCSTM has no composite/submachine element that owns HumanDriving-analog substates; the sole 'Autonomous' state is a flat leaf with no owned initial pseudostate. I also examine NL4.2-CONTAIN-1 (auto final containment) from a behavioral angle: the closed model represents 'AutonomousFinal' as a sibling leaf of Autonomous rather than a state nested within an Autonomous composite, so the auto-final substate is not behaviorally reachable only through the Autonomous composite's internal control -- it is directly reachable from HumanDriving via Power_Off, bypassing Autonomous entirely. This is a distinct wrong_scope containment defect visible in the closed reachability graph. Root reachability itself is intact: all six states are reachable_from_initial=true, so no additional root-reachability defect is warranted beyond the owner-scoped initial-entry issue already derived under NL2 lineage.

The exact source inventory lists all four states with parent=null (flat siblings), and inspection_equivalent_facts.states confirms all five leaf states share the root wrapper as parent, not Autonomous. issues.observed: The exact closed transition AutonomousActive -> HumanDriving triggered by Brake_Pressed (transition:line:18) has guard=null in inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions; there is also no substate-configuration predicate available because AutonomousFinal is not contained in Autonomous/AutonomousActive at all, so 'in (auto final)' has no exact carrier to bind to on this transition.
issues.reason: The bound carrier transition (line 18) has an exact empty guard field while the contract requires an exact non-trivial guard conjunction including a substate-membership condition that has no representable carrier given the containment gap; this is a precise negative fact on an exact existing transition.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the 'brake pressed' event name itself substitutes for a data guard and that 'in (auto final)' is not meant as a formal state-configuration guard but as descriptive context; however the NL explicitly requires this as an exact guard property distinct from the trigger event, and the closed transition's guard field is empty, so the exact required guard content is absent.
issues.title: AutonomousActive->HumanDriving (Brake_Pressed) transition has no guard field and cannot express the required 'in (auto final)' conjunct

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions row for transition:line:19 (source=HumanDriving, target=Autonomous, triggers=[Front_Distance_10_2], guard=null); NL-CONTRACT-NL4-GUARD-1 normative_statement.
issues.expected: The HumanDrivingMode-to-AutonomousMode transition must be guarded by the exact condition front_distance > 10.
issues.observed: The bound closed transition HumanDriving -> Autonomous (transition:line:19) is realized only via the event trigger Front_Distance_10_2 with guard=null in inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions; there is no separate data-guard field carrying the exact predicate front_distance > 10 on this transition.
issues.reason: The bound carrier transition has an exact empty guard field while NL4-GUARD-1 requires an exact guard expression; this is a precise negative fact on an existing transition rather than a missing-edge case.
issues.requirement_quote: when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event name 'Front Distance > 10' textually encodes the same condition as an event label, so one could argue the requirement is satisfied by representing the comparison as an event rather than a formal guard; this is a plausible modeling choice, but the contract specifically requires an exact guard property distinct from the trigger, and the transition's guard field remains empty.
issues.title: HumanDriving->Autonomous transition has no explicit guard field for the required front_distance > 10 condition

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows is_composite=false for Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal, all with parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010 (the root), not parent=Autonomous; fcstm_model.model_ir.state_refs lists these as flat sibling refs; only initial edge in the model is transition:line:13 ([*] -> HumanDriving) at root scope per exact_source_inventory tr_0001 and inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions line 13.
issues.expected: AutonomousMode must be a composite/submachine state that owns child substates (AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, AutonomousFinal) and must have its own initial pseudostate edge entering one of those children when AutonomousMode is entered.
issues.observed: In the closed FCSTM, Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, and AutonomousFinal are all declared as sibling non-composite (is_composite=false) states directly parented by the root wrapper state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0010; there is no composite Autonomous state and therefore no owner-local initial edge from Autonomous into any child substate. The only initial pseudostate edge in the model is transition:line:13 ([*] -> HumanDriving) owned by the root, which is a different scope and does not discharge this owner-scoped obligation.
issues.reason: The NL explicitly requires AutonomousMode to be a sub-machine/composite owning substates with its own default entry; the closed model instead flattens the hierarchy into sibling leaf states parented directly by the root, so no exact owner-local initial edge for Autonomous exists to enter any of AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal, a distinct behavioral consequence of the missing containment.
issues.requirement_quote: The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue HumanDriving->Autonomous (transition:line:14) functionally substitutes as an entry into the autonomous behavior sequence, but that transition targets the flat leaf state Autonomous itself, not a child substate owned by a composite Autonomous; it cannot satisfy an owner-local initial pseudostate edge because no such owning composite exists in the closed model.
issues.title: AutonomousMode has no owned composite state or owner-local initial pseudostate edge in the closed FCSTM

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for AutonomousFinal (parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010, is_composite=false); inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions line 20 (source=HumanDriving, target=AutonomousFinal, trigger=Power_Off) showing a direct reachable path from HumanDriving to AutonomousFinal that never traverses Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive.
issues.expected: The 'auto final' substate must be a descendant contained within the AutonomousMode composite, reachable only through AutonomousMode's internal control flow so that the guard 'in (auto final)' refers to an internal AutonomousMode substate condition.
issues.observed: In the closed FCSTM, AutonomousFinal is a sibling leaf state directly parented by the root wrapper (parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010), not by any Autonomous composite; it is reached directly by transition:line:20 from HumanDriving on Power_Off, entirely bypassing Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive. There is no containment edge placing AutonomousFinal inside AutonomousMode.
issues.reason: The NL ties 'auto final' semantically to AutonomousMode's internal completion condition, but the closed model's flat topology makes AutonomousFinal reachable independently from HumanDriving via Power_Off without ever passing through Autonomous, showing the substate is not actually contained in or gated by the AutonomousMode composite scope.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The flat naming similarity between AutonomousFinal and the Autonomous cluster might suggest an implied grouping, but inspection_equivalent_facts.states explicitly records parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010 for AutonomousFinal, not parent=Autonomous, so no exact containment edge exists to rebut this observation.
issues.title: AutonomousFinal is reachable directly from HumanDriving bypassing AutonomousMode, and is not contained within an AutonomousMode composite in the closed model

branches.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, endpoint/guard fidelity, containment, and default-entry defects across the six NL segments against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) NL2's AutonomousMode composite maps to source/model 'Autonomous' state, but the source inventory and FCSTM both declare Autonomous as a flat simple state with a single outgoing edge to AutonomousIdle -- there is no owner-local initial pseudostate edge into Autonomous's declared substates (AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive), which are siblings of Autonomous rather than contained children. This produces both a containment violation (AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal are not nested inside Autonomous) and an owner-local initial-entry violation (Autonomous has no [*]->child edge). (2) NL4.2's required guard 'brake pressed AND in (auto final)' is not realized: the closed transition AutonomousActive->HumanDriving triggered by Brake_Pressed carries no guard field at all (guard=null), and there is no substate/containment relationship that would let 'in (auto final)' be evaluated, since AutonomousFinal is a sibling flat state, not nested under AutonomousMode/Autonomous. (3) The AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode return transition itself (endpoint) does exist via two edges (line 17 Human_Steering_Cmd, line 18 Brake_Pressed) both AutonomousActive->HumanDriving, so NL4.2-ENDPOINT-1 is satisfied as endpoint existence, but the guard defect and containment defect remain separate issues. (4) NL4.2-CONTAIN-1: 'auto final' (source AutonomousFinal) is required to be contained within AutonomousMode/Autonomous, but source inventory shows AutonomousFinal as a top-level sibling state with parent=null, and FCSTM shows AutonomousFinal parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010 (the root), not Autonomous -- this is an exact wrong_scope containment violation. (5) NL5-TERM/ENDPOINT: HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal edge (line 20/tr_0008) exists satisfying endpoint existence, and AutonomousFinal has zero outgoing transitions (terminal leaf), so termination is structurally not violated by re-entry (no cycle back), satisfying NL5-TERM-1's re-entry check; omit from candidates. (6) NL1, NL3, NL4-ENDPOINT, NL4-GUARD are all satisfied: HumanDriving exists as simple state; root [*]->HumanDriving with Power_On-consuming edge from HumanDriving realizes NL3 (owner=root, target=HumanDriving element_declaration satisfied structurally); HumanDriving->Autonomous edge exists (tr_0007/line19, Front_Distance_10_2 trigger corresponds to front_distance>10), satisfying NL4 endpoint; guard is realized as an event trigger rather than a data guard field (guard=null on transition), which is a precise guard-representation gap -- this remains a candidate since NL4 requires an explicit guard 'front_distance > 10' but FCSTM stores it only as an event name Front_Distance_10_2 with no guard field, so I keep this as a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than omitting it, since the exact frozen guard content is absent.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, stable termination, and derived initial-entry defects. Closed FCSTM shows: root [*] -> HumanDriving (reachable, tr line13), HumanDriving <-> Autonomous reachable pair, AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive reachable, and AutonomousFinal reachable but with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic, verify_facts deadlock check refuted). NL5-TERM-1 requires a genuine terminal transition to a Final state on power-off; the closed model does route HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal on Power_Off and AutonomousFinal has no outgoing edge, so the reachable leaf is a true dead end with no re-entry or cycling -- this satisfies the termination obligation rather than violating it (no re-entry, no exit to another operating scope). All six declared events have a reachable consumer transition per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, so no NL contract here needs an event-consumer-coverage candidate. The composite Autonomous is flat in FCSTM (no owned entry semantics beyond a single transition to AutonomousIdle-like state named Autonomous itself, which is a leaf state, not a submachine with children in the closed model) -- so the NL2-DERIVED-97da8afc74902d28e3c0 owner-local initial-entry obligation cannot be satisfied because the closed model collapses AutonomousMode/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/auto-final into sibling leaf states with no owning composite state and no owner-local initial pseudostate edge for an 'Autonomous' composite. This is the key behavioral defect: AutonomousMode is required as a composite owning substates (NL2-DECL-1, already handled by contract_structure_contrast lens) and required to have an owner-local default entry (derived contract), but the closed FCSTM has no composite/submachine element that owns HumanDriving-analog substates; the sole 'Autonomous' state is a flat leaf with no owned initial pseudostate. I also examine NL4.2-CONTAIN-1 (auto final containment) from a behavioral angle: the closed model represents 'AutonomousFinal' as a sibling leaf of Autonomous rather than a state nested within an Autonomous composite, so the auto-final substate is not behaviorally reachable only through the Autonomous composite's internal control -- it is directly reachable from HumanDriving via Power_Off, bypassing Autonomous entirely. This is a distinct wrong_scope containment defect visible in the closed reachability graph. Root reachability itself is intact: all six states are reachable_from_initial=true, so no additional root-reachability defect is warranted beyond the owner-scoped initial-entry issue already derived under NL2 lineage.
